jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Off the Clock
jokes.joke: I'm a paramedic. My cousin invited me to his wedding reception and said, 'You're off the clock. Just relax!' Then he seated me between his 94-year-old grandfather, who brought an oxygen tank, and Uncle Dave, who thinks an open bar is an endurance event. Everyone else got a plus-one. I got a triage section.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Response Time
jokes.joke: I’m an EMT, so technically my whole job is being the bigger person. But last month the guy who cut me off in traffic called 911 for a splinter. Same guy. I recognized the license plate before I recognized the house. And wouldn’t you know it, my GPS just... struggled that day. Took the scenic route. Hit every light. He’s fine now. Humbled, but fine. I didn’t withhold care. I just really, really honored the speed limit.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Big Day
jokes.joke: I went to my ex-girlfriend’s wedding reception last weekend. I didn’t want to cause a scene, so I just quietly slipped a three-tier cake into the catering tent labeled 'For the Divorce Lawyer.' Look, call me vindictive, but when someone hands you an open bar and a microphone during the toast, you owe it to the room to close strong.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Seating Chart
jokes.joke: I went to a wedding reception last weekend. The bride was so vindictive she arranged the entire seating chart by how badly people had wronged her. I ended up at a table with three of her exes, her former boss, and the guy who once took the last parking spot at Trader Joe’s. By the time the salad came we had already started a support group.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Open Bar Triage
jokes.joke: I worked as an emergency medical responder, so when my cousin got married I thought I'd finally get one night off. Ten minutes into the wedding reception, the DJ yelled, 'Is there a medic here?' and every relative pointed at me like they were trying to win a raffle. I spent the whole evening taking vitals on people who were just dancing to ABBA.

scores.comment: A recognizable revenge premise with effective escalation and a decent speed-limit punchline. The EMT's petty retaliation creates comic tension, but the payoff is somewhat predictable and the opening is awkward.
The divorce-lawyer cake offers an amusing visual, but the microphone and open-bar setup promises a payoff that never arrives. The final sentence substitutes comic bravado for an actual punchline.
The vindictive seating chart is a coherent premise, and the Trader Joe's detail provides a modest laugh. The support-group ending is familiar and predictable rather than a surprising comic turn.

Clear first-person setup, natural progression, and an accessible image of relatives pointing at the medic. The raffle comparison is amusing, but the ABBA punchline feels arbitrary rather than sharply surprising.
